LISTING OF CLAIMS
This listing of claims will replace all prior versions, and listings, of claims in the application:
1. (Currently Amended) A method for fueling and using an aircraft, wherein the method comprises: conditioning a fuel tank, wherein the fuel tank comprises a chamber between an inner wall and an outer wall of the fuel tank, wherein the chamber includes at least one layer of reflective foil within an insulative material, and clean dry gas is pumped into the chamber to aid in insulating a liquid gas fuel; venting the liquid gas fuel from the chamber, wherein a direction of fuel flow is regulated by a liquid check valve to prevent back flow of the vented liquid gas fuel to the fuel tank; storing, using the fuel tank comprising the chamber between the inner wall and the outer wall of the fuel tank, the liquified liquid gas fuel, wherein the chamber is configured to insulate the liquid gas fuel by prevention of condensation of humidity within the fuel tank of the aircraft; fueling, using a fuel line, the aircraft, wherein fueling further comprises: filling the fuel tank with the liquified gas fuel to a desired level, wherein the desired level comprises fuel for a plurality of flights plus reserves, wherein a sensor connected to the fuel tank detects at least abnormal phenomena related insulation of the fuel tank, wherein the sensor is configured to: detect humidity within the fuel tank; and convert the detected at least abnormal phenomena into a signal that is then transmitted to a computing device; and removing, using the computing device, the fuel line as function of the desired level in the aircraft; and preparing the fuel tank for flight as a function of the desired level; and flying, using the aircraft, a plurality of flights using the liquid gas fuel.
2. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the aircraft comprises a blended wing body aircraft.
3. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the fuel tank is configured to have a multi-lobe geometry and comprises an insulation material with a thermal conductivity less than 0.10 W/m-K.
4. (Original) The method of claim 3, wherein the fuel tank comprises a septum.
5. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 3, wherein the multi-lobe geometry provides tension for each fuel tank of the multi-lobe geometry.
6. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 1, wherein the fuel tank is prepared as a function of a fill datum.
7. (Original) The method of claim 1, further comprising venting, using a vent line, the fuel tank, wherein the vent line is in fluid connection to the fuel tank.
8. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the vent line is configured to capture gaseous hydrogen from the fuel tank.
9. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the vent line is configured to release pressure from the fuel tank.
10. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the vent line includes a pressure regulator.
11. (Currently Amended) The method of claim 7, wherein the vent line is insulated to prevent [[the]]an accumulation of frozen gases.
12. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the vent line includes an inner wall and an outer wall wherein a void resides in between.
13. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the vent line further comprises a heat exchanger.
14. (Original) The method of claim 7, wherein the preparing the fuel tank for flight further includes detaching the vent line from the fuel tank as a function of the desired level.
15. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the preparing of the fuel tank for flight further includes detaching the fuel line from the fuel tank as a function of the desired level.
16. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the plurality of flights are further configured to: commence at a first refueling station; and terminate at a second refueling station.
17. (Previously Presented) The method of claim 1, wherein no fueling occurs between the flights of the plurality of flights.
18. (Canceled)
19. (Canceled)
20. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the liquified gas fuel is comprised of liquid hydrogen.
